target.title: fix(tlon): bound Urbit auth response body drain to prevent OOM
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The Urbit login flow in the Tlon extension reads the entire response body via `response.text()` solely to flush the stream so that `set-cookie` headers finalize. The body content is discarded. This call had no size bound — a misconfigured or hostile Urbit endpoint could stream gigabytes into process memory during login.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the unbounded `response.text()` body drain with a **streaming reader with a 64 KiB cumulative drain budget**. When the body stream is available (Node 18+, Bun, Deno), the reader reads chunks until the total drained bytes reach the threshold, then cancels the stream. The 64 KiB threshold is a **cumulative accounting cap** — a single producer chunk may push the total above 64 KiB because we check after each read, which avoids splitting chunks mid-stream. When no body stream is available (rare polyfill/edge case), the fallback `text()` path is preserved for compatibility.

The body content was always discarded; only the `set-cookie` header is consumed.

## User Impact

Urbit login no longer risks OOM from an oversized response body. Normal login flows (small JSON bodies) are completely unaffected. The cookie extraction behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/auth.ssrf.test.ts --run`: **5/5 passed** (2 existing SSRF + 3 new body drain tests).
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- The three new tests cover: streamed body drain with cookie extraction, oversized stream cancellation after the 64 KiB cap, and the body-less fallback path.

### Real behavior proof (loopback drain)

Controlled loopback exercising the same drain pattern used in production:

```json
{"case":"under-cap","drained":1024,"cancelled":false,"cookie":"urbauth-~zod=abc; Path=/; HttpOnly"}
{"case":"over-cap","drained":65536,"cancelled":true,"cookie":"urbauth-~zod=xyz; Path=/; HttpOnly","note":"Stream cancelled after 64 KiB cumulative drain; cookie still available"}
{"case":"body-less-fallback","drained":-1,"cookie":"urbauth-~zod=fallback; Path=/; HttpOnly"}
```

- **Under-cap (1 KiB)**: drains fully, stream completes normally, cookie extracted.
- **Over-cap (256 KiB)**: drains exactly 65536 bytes (64 KiB), stream cancelled, cookie STILL extracted — the drain threshold prevents unbounded buffering without breaking auth.
- **Body-less fallback**: uses `text()` path, cookie extracted.

The 64 KiB threshold is intentionally a **cumulative read budget**, not a strict per-chunk allocation. Since `reader.read()` returns producer-defined chunks, a single chunk may push the total slightly above 64 KiB. This is safe: the threshold prevents unbounded accumulation, and the previous chunk (at most 64 KiB) is released before the next read.
